findings.claim: field() turns any truthy non-list value at a [] path into a list of one, so `sources: src/a.py` (a bare string) or a single sources mapping now yields a resource. The old _sources returned [] for any non-list sources, so review_due now checks git history for concepts it used to skip. The plan says field keeps today's forms; the single-mapping case was only meant for verified.

test_manifesto_marks_i4_enforced checks the log with r'I4.*enforced|`manifesto`' on the last dated section, and the I1/I3 line in that section already contains `manifesto`, so the test passes with the I4 log line deleted. r5's fails_when names a missing log line.

ALLOWED_FIELDS cites the wrong spec sections for two keys: the pinned validator puts `verified` under section 5.2 (5.3 is trust tiers) and root-index `okf_version` under section 12, not 8 (section 8 says a non-root index carries no front matter).

The reads scan only recognises a bare-name front_matter(...) call, so `okf.front_matter(p).get('title')` or an alias such as `fm = front_matter` reads front matter without the test noticing. Nothing in src does this today.

verdict.text: The change does what the plan asks.
All front matter reads in src/kmctl go through okf.field.
The writes test runs every writing verb and checks the keys.
The link regexes now follow CommonMark's angle-bracket rule.
The gates are green.
There are four non-blocking findings: field() now accepts more sources forms than before, the log check in r5 cannot fail, two section citations are wrong, and the reads scan misses attribute calls.
Each has a simple fix that does not need another review.
`loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree: lint, format and tests pass; rows r1 to r5 pass; "stamp green: a4bd7051...".

I read the full staged diff (the changes are staged, not committed) and checked every front matter read: grep shows front_matter called only in concepts, supersede, handoffs and review_due, and each result goes into field().
r1: the test runs init, new for each kind, new handoff with --key twice, new decision, decision supersede and new doc in tmp_path.
It collects nested paths from every .okf and docs page and asserts they are a subset of ALLOWED_FIELDS.
An unknown key written by any of these verbs would fail it.
r2: I ran _bad_reads on probe sources.
It flags `meta.get` after assignment, annotated assignment, walrus, tuple unpacking and keyword use.
It misses `okf.front_matter(...)` and aliases (f4).
r3: the test covers verified as one mapping and as a list, sources with string and mapping items, generated.at, defaults, and KeyError on an unknown key.
A probe shows the non-list sources forms behave differently (f1).
r4: under the old regexes `[x](<a>b.md>)` fell back to the plain target `<a>b.md>`, and `[r]: <a>b.md>` matched `<a>`, so both were reported.
A probe of the new regexes: `[x](<a>b.md>)` gives no match, `<ok.md>`, `plain.md "t"`, `[r]: <ok.md> "t"` and `[r]: plain.md` still resolve, and `[r]: <a>b.md>` gives no match.
r5: the manifesto marks I4 enforced and names the test, and the strict validator runs.
The log assertion is weak (f2).
review_due's helper refactor, the dataclasses.field rename and the handoffs tuple reshaping keep the old behaviour (same defaults for title and description, same sort keys).
I compared the section citations against tests/vendor/okf/okf_validate.py (f3).
f1 (bug, non-blocking): the `[value] if value` wrap in field() applies to every [] path, not only verified.

Non-blocking because it only reads malformed (non-list) sources more leniently, and the fix is plain: limit the single-mapping wrap to verified and keep non-list sources as [], or keep the new behaviour and document and test it.
f2 (test-strength, non-blocking): the log line exists, so nothing is wrong today.
Tighten the regex to require I4 on the same line, for example `I4.*enforced`.
f3 (docs, non-blocking): fix the two citations (verified to 5.2, okf_version to 12).
f4 (test-strength, non-blocking): also match `ast.Attribute` calls whose attr is `front_matter`.
No current code escapes the scan.
The manifesto rule asks that an enforced invariant's test drive kmctl from outside.
The reads half is a source scan, as the signed plan chose.
The writes half drives the CLI.
